label: Free 2.0
title: A physics world that repeats exactly
lede: Lagrangian 2.0 makes the world deterministic: the same bodies, inputs and seed give the same numbers at any frame rate and on any machine. It also adds snapshots, a state hash and the Vue adapter on npm, all MIT.

items.title: Seeded, repeatable runs
items.text: Give the world a seed and use world.random() instead of Math.random(). Two runs with the same seed end in the same state, so tests and replays are reliable.
items.codeTitle: Run it twice with the same seed
items.output:
run 1: af530c07
run 2: af530c07
seed 8: f254a889

items.title: Same result at every frame rate
items.text: The world always simulates in fixed steps, and sleeping and sensors are decided in every step. A 30 Hz, 60 Hz or 144 Hz display no longer changes the outcome.
items.codeTitle: Advance the same world in frames of different length
items.output:
30 Hz frames, 4 s: af530c07 time 4
60 Hz frames, 4 s: af530c07 time 4
144 Hz frames, 4 s: af530c07 time 4

items.title: Snapshot, restore and replay
items.text: world.snapshot() returns plain JSON for bodies, clock and random generator. Restore it later and the run continues exactly as before, handy for undo, saved scenes and regression tests.
items.codeTitle: Save at 2 s, run on, rewind, run again
items.output:
time after restore: 2
replayed hash matches: true

items.title: Keep the 1.x timing while you update
items.text: Fixed steps change when a body falls asleep or a sensor fires by a frame or two in some scenes. legacyStepping restores the 1.x behaviour as a bridge. It is removed in 2.1.
items.code: const world = new World({ bounds, legacyStepping: true });
items.outputTitle: Same scene with legacyStepping: true (hash differs from the 2.0 run above)

items.title: Vue adapter is on npm
items.text: @sweberdev/lagrangian-vue, the composables for springs, dragging, scrolling and the world in Vue 3, is now published at 2.0.0 next to the core, React and Svelte packages.

note: Node 22 or newer is needed to build. world.step(dt) now also settles and senses, so a hand-stepped world matches a running one.
